memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Lead Near Highs; JPM and UNH Breaking Down on Relative Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market right now. NVDA sits just 0.8% off its 52-week high with strong 12-week relative strength of +13% vs SPY, while MSFT has been the standout performer with an extraordinary +32.3% 12-week relative strength and only a -4.5% drawdown from highs. On the other side, JPM's RSI at 34.5 and -8.2% four-week return signal a deteriorating trend that has broken below its 50-day mean by 5.6%, and UNH is in a similar downtrend with -13.8% over 12 weeks and -16.2% relative strength vs SPY over the same period. I have highest conviction in the NVDA and MSFT longs given their proximity to highs and persistent relative strength, and I would avoid JPM until it reclaims its 50-day average (roughly $352).

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power dominates; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I see the strongest fundamental setups in NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, and MSFT, where revenue growth ranges from +17.7% to +105.9% YoY and net margins sit between 31% and 62%, reflecting durable and expanding earnings power. NVDA's 2027Q2 quarter is extraordinary—$96.2B revenue (+106% YoY) with a 62% net margin and only $33.4B total debt—making it the clearest earnings compounder in the universe. GOOGL posted a 93.7% net margin on $119.8B revenue with just $14.8B of debt, though I want to understand the one-time items driving that margin before sizing up further. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to 4.9%, and PG's net income declined 15.8% on anemic 1.5% revenue growth—both signal deteriorating earnings quality. I would revisit XOM if Q2 margins recover above 8% and PG if organic revenue growth reaccelerates above 3%.

views.note: Revenue +106% YoY, 62% net margin, and modest $33.4B debt make this the highest-quality earnings trajectory in the universe.
24% revenue growth and 93.7% net margin on minimal debt are compelling, though the margin level likely includes one-time items that need clarification.
Full-year 10-K shows $90B quarterly revenue (+17.7% YoY), 39.7% net margin, and manageable $40.3B debt—steady durable compounder.
Net income surged 245% YoY to $62.7B on $200.6B revenue, lifting net margin to 31.2%, though $133B total debt bears monitoring.
Revenue +16.4% and 27.2% net margin are solid but $82.3B debt is elevated; I need to see Services mix and FCF detail before getting constructive.
Net income +41% YoY and 36.9% margin are strong for a bank, but $460.5B total debt and credit-cycle sensitivity keep me neutral.
Revenue +24% YoY with 17.5% net margin and net income +65% show cyclical upswing; would reassess if revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) and only 4.9% net margin on $73.3B debt, though net income rebounded 61%—need sustained top-line growth to get constructive.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B with a 4.9% net margin on flat revenue—clear earnings compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue grew just 1.5% while net income fell 15.8%, compressing net margin to 14.4%—no durable earnings growth visible here.

memos.headline: Stagflationary Tilt: 10y at 5.28% With CPI at 3.4% YoY Argues Against Duration and For Defensives
memos.body: I see a regime that is best described as a hawkish pause turning into a mild re-tightening: the fed funds upper bound has risen 25bp over three months to 4.00%, while 12-month CPI is running at 3.4%—well above target—and the 10y yield has surged 118bp year-over-year to 5.28%. The labor market remains firm with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons, which removes any urgency for the Fed to ease and may even justify the recent hike. The 10y-2y spread at +46bp is positive but has steepened 15bp in three months, consistent with term-premium repricing rather than growth optimism. This environment is hostile to long-duration growth equities and favors short-duration cash-flow generators, banks benefiting from a steep curve and high rates, and energy names with real-asset backing. A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would shift my regime call toward easing expectations and make me more constructive on growth.

views.note: High-multiple duration equity faces headwinds from 10y yields at 5.28% and no near-term easing catalyst.
Extreme duration sensitivity at these yield levels; 118bp YoY rise in the 10y compresses growth multiples aggressively.
Quality cash flows provide some buffer but still a long-duration asset in a 5.28% 10y world; not compelling either way.
Positive and steepening 10y-2y spread at 46bp plus a 4.00% fed funds rate supports net interest margins and bank earnings.
Real-asset energy name acts as an inflation hedge with CPI at 3.4% YoY and short duration profile suits the rate regime.
Defensive staple with pricing power in a 3.4% CPI environment; lower beta helps if rate shock triggers broader equity weakness.
Consumer-facing cyclical growth name doubly exposed to rate-driven multiple compression and potential consumer squeeze from sticky inflation.
Cyclical beneficiary of firm employment at 4.1% but rising rates threaten capex spending; offsetting forces keep me on the sideline.
Ad-driven model is somewhat cyclical; strong labor market helps ad spend but 5.28% 10y weighs on valuation—net neutral.
Defensive healthcare with low duration and steady cash flows is well-suited to a hawkish-pause, above-target-inflation regime.

memos.headline: NVDA Earnings Beat Drove +8.7% Pop; Rest of Universe Shows Routine Filing Activity With No Clear Sentiment Shift
memos.body: I see one standout signal in the universe this cycle: NVDA's Q2 results filed 2026-08-26 triggered an +8.7% overnight move, and subsequent 8-Ks on material agreements and other events suggest continued positive narrative momentum with high coverage volume. For the rest of the universe, the filing activity is largely procedural—AAPL and AMZN each disclosed director/officer changes, MSFT issued a Reg FD disclosure, and CAT entered a new debt obligation, none of which signal a decisive tone shift. UNH's Reg FD filing and GOOGL's 'Other Events' 8-K from August are similarly low-signal from a media-tone perspective. I have conviction that NVDA's positive sentiment has further room to run given the earnings catalyst, but I am cautious that the +8.7% move may already price in much of the good news; elsewhere I see no actionable sentiment divergence.

views.note: Strong earnings beat with +8.7% price reaction and follow-on material agreements suggest positive narrative momentum, though some of the move is likely priced.
Director/officer change via 8-K/A is routine and carries no discernible sentiment signal.
Two 8-Ks covering officer changes and other events are procedural with no tone inflection.
New material agreement and direct financial obligation filing is standard capital-markets activity; no negative or positive tone shift detected.
Reg FD disclosure alone provides insufficient signal to form a directional sentiment view.
Reg FD filing is informational with no evidence of a narrative shift in media tone.
August 'Other Events' 8-K is stale and generic; no sentiment edge.

memos.headline: Oil at $100 and Widening Credit Spreads Signal Energy-Supply Stress; NVDA Export-Control Risk Persists
memos.body: I see a divergent macro picture from a geopolitical lens: the economic policy uncertainty index has dropped sharply (156 vs ~196 a month ago), yet WTI crude has surged 43% over three months to nearly $100/bbl, and HY OAS has widened 50 bp over the same window to 3.24%. The oil spike suggests a structural supply disruption—likely tied to Middle East or sanctions-related tightening—rather than a demand-driven move, given that credit is simultaneously deteriorating. NVDA filed two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3), which in the current export-control environment I read as potential disclosure of new China-related restrictions or customer-notification events; I lack the full text but the cadence is unusual and warrants caution. For energy-exposed names like XOM, the commodity tailwind is obvious but I note that policy uncertainty is falling, meaning the current price regime may already be priced as semi-permanent rather than a shock premium. I have moderate conviction on the energy and semiconductor policy vectors but lower conviction on the broader credit-widening signal until I see whether it stabilizes.

views.note: WTI near $100 with a 43% 3-month surge provides a strong earnings tailwind; supply-side tightness appears structural rather than transient.
Two 8-K filings in three weeks amid ongoing export-control scrutiny raises the probability of incremental China revenue headwinds; would revisit if filings prove benign.
No direct policy catalyst in the evidence, but China supply-chain concentration remains a background risk with oil-driven input-cost pressure.
Sep 14 8-K is opaque but rising energy costs and widening HY spreads could pressure logistics margins; no clear directional call.
Steepening yield curve (+15 bp over 3 months) supports NII, but 50 bp HY OAS widening hints at rising credit losses; net effect roughly neutral from a geopolitical-risk standpoint.
Energy capex cycle could benefit CAT, but elevated oil also raises input costs; policy uncertainty decline is mildly positive for infrastructure spending.
